rounds.text: CG-VAK Software & Exports Ltd is currently exhibiting a concerning trend of deteriorating growth, as evidenced by a 1% contraction in compounded sales growth over both the three-year and trailing twelve-month periods [E16, E17]. This stagnation is mirrored in the bottom line, where compounded profit growth has declined by 7% over three years and 12% over the trailing twelve months [E20, E21]. The market has reacted to this lack of momentum with significant pessimism, as the stock has suffered a 32% decline over three years and a 37% drop over the past year [E24, E25]. Furthermore, the company’s recent quarterly operating margin has compressed by 1 percentage point compared to the year-ago quarter, and the overall quarterly margin trend is inconsistent [E31, E33]. While the company maintains a low debt profile, its return on equity has been low at 13.8% over the last three years [E37, E54]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong cash conversion ratio of 1.57x and is trading below its book value [E34, E52].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over the last three years and the trailing twelve months is -1% [E16, E17], and compounded profit growth over those same periods has fallen by 7% and 12% [E20, E21]. However, this near-term softness masks a remarkably resilient longer-term compounding profile where 10-year profit growth sits at 22% [E18]. Conceded: the stock price has dropped 32% over three years and 37% over one year [E24, E25], but this reaction is overly punitive given that fundamentals are outpacing the stock and profit growth has recently exceeded 1-year price growth by 25% [E47, E48]. Conceded: quarterly operating margin declined by 1 percentage point and the quarterly trend is inconsistent [E31, E33], yet the broader yearly operating-margin trend has been increasing over the last four years, reaching 20% in the TTM [E30, E32]. Conceded: return on equity has been low at 13.8% over the last three years [E54], but median ROE stands at a healthy 17% over both 5-year and 10-year horizons [E26, E27]. Finally, the bear's anxiety over financial stability is entirely misplaced because the company is nearly debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.02x, alongside pristine cash generation featuring a 1.57x cash conversion ratio and ₹ 14.53 Cr in free cash flow for Mar 2026 [E34, E36, E37, E51].
